title: Ποιμὴν ⟨λύκον εἰς μάνδραν εἰσάγων⟩ καὶ κύων
titleEn: The Shepherd Bringing a Wolf into the Fold, and the Dog
part: The Shepherd Bringing a Wolf into the Fold, and the Dog (Chambry 317)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 317. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t:
Μάνδρας ἔσω πρόβατα ποιμὴν εἰσάγων
μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ λύκον ἤμελλε συγκλεῖσαι,
εἰ μὴ ⟨ὁ⟩ κύων ἰδὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν·
« Πῶς τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης θέλων σῶσαι
τόνδε τὸν λύκον συνεισάγεις τῇ ποίμνῃ ; »
sentences.tr:
Mandras esō probata poimēn eisagōn
met’ autōn kai lykon ēmelle synkleisai,
ei mē ⟨ho⟩ kyōn idōn pros auton eipen·
« Pōs ta probata tēs poimnēs thelōn sōsai
tonde ton lykon syneisageis tēi poimnēi ; »
sentences.l: A shepherd, bringing sheep inside the fold, was about to shut a wolf in along with them, had not ⟨the⟩ dog, seeing it, said to him: « How is it that, wishing to save the sheep of the flock, you are bringing this wolf in along with the flock? »
sentences.i: A shepherd bringing his sheep into the fold was on the point of shutting a wolf in with them, had the dog not seen it and said to him: « How is it that, when you want to save the sheep of your flock, you are bringing this wolf in among them? »
sentences.n: Chambry sets the body of this fable as verse — five short lines of twelve syllables each — his source here being the verse tradition rather than the prose collection; the moral below is printed as prose. Μάνδρας ἔσω puts the adverb after the genitive it governs, a liberty verse allows. ἤμελλε … εἰ μή is the Greek 'he was on the point of doing it, had not …', where English wants an 'if' clause first. ⟨ὁ⟩ is Chambry's own supplement of the article, marked with the angle brackets he uses for words he adds; it fills out the line.

sentences.t: Ὅτι μεγίστην βλάβην καὶ θανάτου παραιτίαν οἶδε ποιεῖν τῶν κακῶν ἡ συνοίκησις.
sentences.tr: Hoti megistēn blabēn kai thanatou paraitian oide poiein tōn kakōn hē synoikēsis.
sentences.l: That living together with the wicked knows how to work the greatest harm, and a part-cause of death.
sentences.i: The story shows that living together with the wicked knows how to work the greatest harm, and to have a hand in bringing death.
sentences.n: The moral opens with a bare Ὅτι, 'that…', and no introducing verb is printed; the governing 'The story shows' is unexpressed in the Greek and is supplied in the idiomatic line. οἶδε with the infinitive is 'knows how to', the ordinary way of saying what a thing habitually does. παραίτιος is the part-cause, the thing with a hand in the result, not the cause simply. συνοίκησις is the sharing of a dwelling, and τῶν κακῶν is the genitive of those one shares it with.
